newsitem.title: USA: Q2 motherboard chip sales $7.5 bln - report.
newsitem.headline: Q2 motherboard chip sales $7.5 bln - report.

text.p: Worldwide revenue for semiconductors installed in personal computers and digital assistant motherboards totaled $7.5 billion in the second quarter, a technology industry researcher reported on Monday.
International Data Corp said the total was down 27.9 percent from the first quarter.

It said price cuts for dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips, static random access memory (SRAM) chips and Flash memory chips pushed motherboard semiconductor revenues down, even though unit shipments and average memory per unit rose.
IDC said DRAM revenues were off 46.1 percent from the first quarter, and SRAM revenues were off 28.5 percent.
IDC predicted motherboard semiconductor revenues would total $32.9 billion for 1996, down 4.1 percent from the $34.3 billion recorded in 1995.

"We believe over the next six months we'll see manufacturers continuing to add more memory to their base systems," said Kelly Henry, IDC analyst. "PC motherboard memory sizes could go up to 24 and even 32 megabytes. At the same time, PC manufacturers will have a little more margin."
The greatest year-over-year revenue gain was made by digital signal processors (DSPs), as they were added to many PC, personal digital assitant (PDA), and hand-held organizers.

By motherboard type, PDA motherboard semiconductor revenue of $21.5 million in the second quarter experienced the smallest decline from the first quarter and were up 75.7 percent over the 1995 second quarter.
Slight second quarter over first quarter gains were made for microcontrollers, programmable logic and non-volatile memory.
